name: Naaman (Syrian army commander)
title: The Healed Gentile
summary: Naaman was the commander of the Syrian king's army and a mighty warrior, but he suffered from leprosy. Through the testimony of an Israelite slave girl and the ministry of the prophet Elisha, he was healed and came to believe in the God of Israel. His story is an early example of God's grace toward Gentile nations.

keyEvents.title: The Testimony of the Israelite Slave Girl
keyEvents.description: A young Israelite girl who served Naaman's wife told about the prophet in Samaria who could heal leprosy. This set Naaman on his journey toward healing.

keyEvents.title: Naaman Comes to Elisha
keyEvents.description: Naaman traveled to Israel with gifts and a letter from the king of Syria. Elisha sent word that he should wash seven times in the Jordan River.

keyEvents.title: Naaman's Anger and Humility
keyEvents.description: At first, Naaman was angry at Elisha's simple instruction, but his servants persuaded him to obey. He washed in the Jordan and was completely healed.

keyEvents.title: The Confession of Faith in the God of Israel
keyEvents.description: After being healed, Naaman returned to Elisha and confessed that there is no God in all the world except in Israel. He asked to take some soil from Israel with him.

keyEvents.title: Elisha Refuses Gifts
keyEvents.description: Naaman offered rich gifts to Elisha, but the prophet refused to accept anything. This showed that God's grace cannot be bought.

keyEvents.title: Jesus Uses Naaman as an Example
keyEvents.description: In the synagogue at Nazareth, Jesus mentioned Naaman as an example of how God showed grace to Gentiles when Israel rejected the prophets.
